askGeneBridge.title: Ask GeneBridge
askGeneBridge.a1: Sickle cell trait means a person carries one changed copy of the gene for haemoglobin and one typical copy. People with the trait are usually healthy.
askGeneBridge.q2: Does my result mean our baby will be sick?
askGeneBridge.a2: I can't interpret your personal result. A genetic counsellor can explain what it means for you and {partner}.

hero.heading: You carry one copy of the sickle cell gene change (HbAS).

standard.body: This is called sickle cell trait. You are healthy and you don't need treatment.
standard.small: It may matter when planning children, and only if your partner also carries a change in the same gene.

simple.body: This is called sickle cell trait. You are healthy. You do not need treatment.
simple.small: It may matter if you plan to have children and your partner also has it.

hero.geneAria: Two gene copies: one typical copy (A) and one changed copy (S)

risk.title: A risk is not a diagnosis

trait.title: Sickle cell trait (you)
trait.body: One changed copy. Healthy, no symptoms. Can pass the copy on.

disease.title: Sickle cell disease
disease.body: Two changed copies. A lifelong condition that needs medical care.

everyone.title: Everyone carries something
everyone.body: Most people carry a few gene changes without ever knowing. Finding yours means you can plan with information instead of worry.
everyone.cta: What could this mean for children?

quiz.title: Check your understanding
quiz.subtitle: 3 quick questions · not a test

q1.question: Does a carrier result mean you are ill?
q1.explain: A carrier result does not mean you are ill. You are healthy.

q2.question: Is the chance the same for every pregnancy?
q2.explain: Each pregnancy has the same chance, no matter what happened in earlier ones.

q3.question: Who can explain what your result means for your family?
q3.explain: A genetic counsellor can explain what your result means for you and your family.

quiz.needAll: Choose an answer for each question first.
quiz.askCounsellor: A genetic counsellor can go through anything that feels unclear.

main.title: Your shared chances, for each pregnancy
main.subtitle: You are both carriers of sickle cell trait (HbAS).
main.notice: These chances are the same for every pregnancy. Having one affected child doesn’t make the next one less or more likely.
main.info: This is information, not a recommendation. Every option is valid, and the decision is yours.
main.pausedBody: Shared chances show once both of you are sharing result summaries. You can change this at any time.
